8bZh5LMaSmE.summary: Sandi Metz takes an ugly section of conditional code and refactors it into a few simple objects, bridging object-oriented theory and practice. The talk includes her take on the Gilded Rose refactoring kata and the idea that duplication is cheaper than the wrong abstraction.
8bZh5LMaSmE.why: HN treats it as a top-tier programming talk for learning refactoring and for the wrong-abstraction principle, recommended repeatedly over a decade.

8aGhZQkoFbQ.summary: Philip Roberts explains the JavaScript event loop, call stack, callbacks and asynchronous behavior with live visualizations using a tool he built. It demystifies terms like non-blocking and single-threaded.
8aGhZQkoFbQ.why: HN commenters repeatedly name it as the best explanation of the JS event loop and the first thing to watch before tackling async code.

8pTEmbeENF4.summary: Bret Victor's DBX 2013 talk, delivered in the guise of a 1973 IBM engineer with an overhead projector. It surveys forgotten ideas from 1960s and early 70s computing and warns against assuming you know what you're doing.
8pTEmbeENF4.why: HN treats it as a classic, near-mandatory talk on how programming tools and paradigms stagnated and which older ideas deserve revival.

8--5LwHRhjk.summary: Inigo Quilez live-codes a cartoon character painting entirely from math, using signed distance fields in a Shadertoy shader. He explains each step of building the image from formulas.
8--5LwHRhjk.why: HN repeatedly calls it a mind-blowing and accessible introduction to SDFs and procedural art from a master explainer.

8SkdfdXWYaI.summary: Tavis Rudd describes how RSI forced him to program by voice, and shows the Python and Emacs Lisp system he built with voice recognition. A live demo creates and deploys a small system without touching the keyboard.
8SkdfdXWYaI.why: Recurs in threads about RSI, accessibility and voice coding as the go-to demo of a custom spoken command language.

8X69_42Mj-g.summary: Christian Schafmeister's Google Tech Talk on designing spiroligomer molecules and building Clasp, a Common Lisp on LLVM that interoperates with C++, to program molecular design. It covers the chemistry, automatic differentiation for force fields, and how the compiler is built.
8X69_42Mj-g.why: HN repeatedly cites it as a striking example of Common Lisp used to push the frontier of science, and as one of the most inspiring tech talks.

8hAw1z8GdE8.summary: A Google Tech Talk by sleep researcher Dr. William Dement on healthy sleep and performance. He argues sleep debt must be repaid and describes the three characteristics of healthy sleep.
8hAw1z8GdE8.why: HN has recommended it for years as the most useful and entertaining talk on sleep, often to people struggling with tiredness or productivity.

8Ab3ArE8W3s.summary: Jack Rusher's Strange Loop 2022 talk argues that most programming languages are still designed around punchcard-era assumptions. He makes the case for live, interactive programming environments, drawing on Lisp, Smalltalk and REPL-driven development.
8Ab3ArE8W3s.why: HN returns to it constantly as the talk on live programming and what modern tooling is missing, though a few found it too much.

8Z685OF-PS8.summary: Van Jacobson's 2006 Google Tech Talk argues that networking should be rethought around named data rather than host-to-host conversations. He contrasts the circuit and datagram views of the internet and sketches content-centric networking as a replacement for the location-centric TCP/IP model.
8Z685OF-PS8.why: HN commenters point to it as a clear explanation of why data-centric networking fits how the internet is actually used, and as a core talk on content addressing.

8xJzHq8ru0M.summary: Chris McCord's ElixirConf EU 2019 keynote introducing Phoenix LiveView, which builds interactive server-rendered apps without writing JavaScript. It explains how only changed dynamic parts are sent over a websocket.
8xJzHq8ru0M.why: HN recommends it as the primary source for understanding LiveView's advantages and its middle ground between multipage apps and SPAs.

8X7Ng75e5gQ.summary: Russian-American journalist Vladimir Pozner lectures at Yale on how US foreign policy toward Russia after the Soviet collapse shaped Putin, then takes audience questions on election interference, the Skripal poisoning and media independence.
8X7Ng75e5gQ.why: During the 2022 Ukraine war threads, HN commenters recommended it as a non-Western perspective on Russia-West relations and Putin's motives.

826HMLoiE_o.summary: A clip from Attenborough's Life of Mammals following a San tribesman in the Kalahari on an eight-hour persistence hunt, running down a kudu through harsh heat. It shows tracking, endurance running and the hunter's reaction after the kill.
826HMLoiE_o.why: HN returns to it as the canonical footage of persistence hunting in threads about human endurance running and evolution.

8S0FDjFBj8o.summary: Will Stephen's humorous six-minute TEDx talk shows presentation techniques that make you sound brilliant while saying essentially nothing.
8S0FDjFBj8o.why: HN recommends it as a funny deconstruction of TED talk style, and as a favorite example of the appearance of meaning without content.

8fi7uSYlOdc.summary: Liz Rice live-codes a minimal container runtime in a few lines of Go at GOTO Amsterdam 2018. She explains namespaces, control groups and what a host knows about its containers.
8fi7uSYlOdc.why: HN considers it one of the best talks for understanding how containers work from the ground up.

8An2SxNFvmU.summary: A short satirical 'motivational' talk by the character Self-help Singh, a sham life coach who urges viewers to do nothing. It parodies self-help gurus and hustle culture.
8An2SxNFvmU.why: HN commenters recommend it as funny anti-motivational comedy that also touches on real truths about productivity and the rat race.

8JOD1AQGqEg.summary: Dylan Beattie's entertaining NDC talk imagines an alternate history of the web, asking what if different decisions had been made on operating systems, browsers and standards. It blends real history with humor.
8JOD1AQGqEg.why: HN commenters strongly recommend it as a fun alt-history of the web and bring it up whenever people muse about how the web could have been different.

8Ko3TdPy0TU.summary: Matt Parker analyzes the Minecraft speedrunning controversy in which Dream was accused of cheating via improbably lucky drops. He walks through the probability and the statistical arguments in the original accusation and the reply.
8Ko3TdPy0TU.why: HN recommends it as an engaging lesson in probability and in how statistics can expose cheating.

8TjGAWxL23c.summary: A KQED Truly CA documentary narrated by John Waters about the Salton Sea, a once-glamorous California vacation spot now home to an eccentric community. It covers the area's economic, political and environmental problems and features Salvation Mountain.
8TjGAWxL23c.why: HN recommends it as an engaging, funny and fascinating documentary, and cites it in threads on the Salton Sea's history and environmental decline.

8fHi36dvTdE.summary: Leonard Bernstein's 1973 Norton Lectures at Harvard, starting with Musical Phonology. He draws analogies between music and linguistics, including references to Chomsky.
8fHi36dvTdE.why: HN recommends it for a deep theory of why music sounds the way it does.

8wlld3Z9wRc.summary: Explains induced demand beyond roads, showing that it applies to transit, walking and cycling infrastructure too but with different consequences. It corrects common misunderstandings of the concept.
8wlld3Z9wRc.why: HN recommends it as a clear treatment of induced demand across transport modes whenever threads debate road expansion versus transit.

816VLQNdPMM.summary: Rick Beato argues that adults cannot develop true perfect pitch, which he ties to critical-period brain plasticity and language acquisition. He says it can only be developed in young children, and discusses the research behind this.
816VLQNdPMM.why: HN points to it as the standard explanation of why perfect pitch is a childhood window, in threads about absolute pitch training.

85ZCTuekjGA.summary: The first part of Robert Baruch's series on building a 6800 CPU on an FPGA with nMigen, a Python-based hardware description language. It introduces the HDL while implementing a simpler 6800 core.
85ZCTuekjGA.why: HN recommends the series as a practical introduction to nMigen and formal verification for CPU design.

86Krv3gE-c4.summary: The first installment of a hobbyist's video diary documenting his build of a giant walking spider-like vehicle. The footage is casual and self-shot, following the early stages of the project.
86Krv3gE-c4.why: HN commenters point to it as the start of a gripping, wonder-inducing build saga by a prolific maker of ambitious mechanical projects.

8ORLN_KwAgs.summary: PBS Space Time explains the quantum eraser experiment, in which erasing which-path information appears to reverse causality in a double-slit setup. It discusses what this means for quantum mechanics.
8ORLN_KwAgs.why: HN recommends it as a quick introduction to the quantum eraser and delayed choice weirdness, though one commenter notes later corrections to its framing.

86gyW0vUmVs.summary: Permaculture instructor Andrew Millison visits the chinampas, the floating gardens of Xochimilco in Mexico City. He looks at this ancient Aztec agricultural system and the project restoring it.
86gyW0vUmVs.why: HN recommends it as a clear introduction to chinampas and an example of productive agroforestry.

87jfTIWosBw.summary: Joseph White, creator of PICO-8, retraces the design of the fantasy console and how tools can shape and guide creative work. He discusses cozy, constrained design spaces and the influence of user-made cartridges.
87jfTIWosBw.why: HN points to it for the design philosophy behind PICO-8's constraints.

8BIcAZxFfrc.summary: hbomberguy's long video dissects the anti-vaccine movement, analyzing Andrew Wakefield's fraudulent MMR-autism study, the media's role and Wakefield's loss of his license. It combines detailed research with humor.
8BIcAZxFfrc.why: HN commenters call it the definitive, thorough answer to whether vaccines cause autism and recommend it as an entertaining deep dive.

8CAafjodkyE.summary: Kristy Viers demonstrates the iPhone Magnifier combined with VoiceOver to describe the user's surroundings. She shows how the built-in feature reports scenes, faces and lighting.
8CAafjodkyE.why: HN recommends it to show what on-device accessibility features can do and how blind users actually use an iPhone.

8COaMKbNrX0.summary: David Epstein argues in this TED talk that improving athletic records owe much to technology, training and the selection of specialized body types, not just humans getting inherently better. He gives counter-intuitive examples across sports.
8COaMKbNrX0.why: HN links it in threads about athlete body types, sports technology and record-breaking as a relevant, counter-intuitive explanation.

8JrqH2oOTK4.summary: DIY Perks shows how to turn old or smashed TVs and monitors into realistic artificial window lights, using the backlight and Fresnel lens to simulate distant daylight.
8JrqH2oOTK4.why: HN points to it in threads on artificial sunlight, as a buildable and surprisingly convincing artificial window.

8PwwRR8deHk.summary: Part one of Look Mum No Computer's series on buying a whole church pipe organ, covering how it was removed from its home. The series goes on to restoring it and rewiring it for MIDI.
8PwwRR8deHk.why: HN recommends the series as great fun, following a talented and enthusiastic amateur rebuilding a pipe organ.

8455KEDitpU.summary: Tony Heller presents a short video arguing that climate science relies on data truncation, cherry-picking and selective presentation of statistics. It is a one-sided polemic against mainstream climate claims.
8455KEDitpU.why: Shared by climate-skeptic commenters as a counter-argument to alarmist statistics, a contested source rather than consensus.

8AHCfZTRGiI.summary: The official music video for Johnny Cash's cover of Nine Inch Nails' Hurt, from his American Recordings era, filmed late in his life. It is a stark, emotional performance of the song.
8AHCfZTRGiI.why: HN commenters hold it up as one of the greatest cover versions ever, so powerful that Trent Reznor said the song was no longer his.

8FpigqfcvlM.summary: Egoraptor's Sequelitis compares Mega Man Classic and Mega Man X, analyzing how the games teach players through level design without explicit tutorials. It mixes comedy with design analysis.
8FpigqfcvlM.why: HN commenters use it as the standard example of invisible onboarding and good game design, praising it as funny and insightful.

8YUWDrLazCg.summary: Tom Scott makes the difference between a million and a billion dollars tangible by using distance on a road trip instead of volume. The drive makes the scale of a billion intuitively felt.
8YUWDrLazCg.why: HN points to it whenever discussion turns to billionaire wealth or the human difficulty of grasping very large numbers.

8ptH79R53c0.summary: John Lin reveals a rewritten voxel engine demonstrated in a Crystal Islands scene, with much finer voxel detail, fast collision, fracture and path-traced global illumination.
8ptH79R53c0.why: HN cites it as a showcase of one of the best voxel engines, impressive for its detail and smoothness.

8vWaawiUteM.summary: A long George Hotz livestream in which he explores the coronavirus genome and molecular biology from scratch using a browser and Python, hacking on the science in real time.
8vWaawiUteM.why: HN suggests it for coders curious how an outsider approaches coronavirus biology, though it is described as unscientific.

8QiPFmIMxFc.summary: Bret Victor's talk "Inventing on Principle" argues that creators should find a guiding principle to fight for. He shows demos of immediate-feedback tools, such as live-updating code and animation editors.
8QiPFmIMxFc.why: HN recommends it as an inspiring talk on immediate feedback and on living by a principle.

8SF_h3xF3cE.summary: Lesson 1 of fast.ai's Practical Deep Learning for Coders, taught by Jeremy Howard. It takes coders from running code in a Jupyter notebook straight into training a real image model.
8SF_h3xF3cE.why: HN considers the course one of the best hands-on ways into deep learning, praising the code-first teaching style.

8XUutFBbUrg.summary: Markus Triska tours Prolog's most distinctive features, including its use as a database and query language, rule processing, constraint solving and compile-time rewriting. It also covers concise meta-interpreters.
8XUutFBbUrg.why: HN recommends it as the best short introduction to what makes Prolog unique.

8b7erU_DOfE.summary: A Hagerty documentary on a 1979 Lamborghini Countach LP400 S and how it ended the Cannonball Baker Sea-to-Shining-Sea Memorial Trophy Dash. It tells the story of the illicit race started by Brock Yates and its Hollywood adaptation.
8b7erU_DOfE.why: Recommended as a history-rich look at the Cannonball Run and the rebellious philosophy behind it.

8dhp_20j0Ys.summary: Pixar staff tell the story of how Toy Story 2 was almost deleted from the studio's computers and was saved by a home computer backup.
8dhp_20j0Ys.why: HN shares it as a classic backup and operations cautionary tale.

8gw0rXPMMPE.summary: Microsoft's short announcement video for the new Windows Terminal, a modern terminal app for Command Prompt, PowerShell and WSL. It is a stylized trailer for the unreleased project.
8gw0rXPMMPE.why: Mentioned for its unusually polished, nerdy trailer style, and as an example of a good developer tool announcement.

8AyHH9G9et0.summary: Retired Major Brian Shul tells the story of a ground speed check with LA Center while flying the SR-71 Blackbird. He recounts it live at the Hiller Aviation Museum.
8AyHH9G9et0.why: Shared as the pilot's own telling of a famous, amusing SR-71 anecdote that never gets old.

8CMxDNuuAiQ.summary: Juan Benet gives an overview and demo of the go-ipfs alpha. It shows the peer-to-peer content-addressed protocol in action, including streaming video from a home computer.
8CMxDNuuAiQ.why: HN lists it among the best early resources for learning what IPFS is and does.

8FQhtMrUQlE.summary: The full webcast of SpaceX's Falcon 1 Flight 4, the first privately developed liquid-fueled rocket to reach orbit, on 28 September 2008. It includes the crew's cheering and Elon Musk's statement afterward.
8FQhtMrUQlE.why: HN shares it as a nostalgic, historic moment, noting the cheers at each milestone and Musk's address to employees.

8LGDM9exlZw.summary: A 32C3 talk dissecting Red Star OS, North Korea's state-built operating system. The speakers explain its internals and how it invades users' privacy, including file watermarking.
8LGDM9exlZw.why: HN points to it as a deep dive into the surveillance features of North Korea's OS and the extent of that state's digital tracking.

8PmM6SUn7Es.summary: A Kurzgesagt explainer asking whether organic food is really healthier or better for the environment. It defines what organic means and looks at pesticide use, nutrition and environmental impact, with sources.
8PmM6SUn7Es.why: Cited as a sourced overview of what organic means and how it compares on pesticides and nutrition.

8S3B8a8N83k.summary: Dan Wood reviews the Vampire 2 FPGA accelerator for the Amiga 600. He covers how much faster it makes the machine and what it can run.
8S3B8a8N83k.why: Recommended as a decent introduction to the Vampire accelerator and a cheaper way to modernize classic Amigas.

8T6ClX-y2AE.summary: David Weston's BlueHat IL 2023 talk traces the evolution of Windows security and previews Windows 11 and hardware advances. It ends with upcoming changes such as Rust in the kernel and fonts, signed binaries and adminless Windows.
8T6ClX-y2AE.why: HN uses it as the primary source for Microsoft's Rust adoption and its reasoning on TPM and security requirements.

8VqXBA-sGHA.summary: California Superbike School demonstrates its 'No B.S.' bike, which has fixed handlebars so riders can only steer with body lean. It illustrates how little control that gives compared with countersteering.
8VqXBA-sGHA.why: HN recommends it as an eye-opening demonstration of why countersteering matters on two wheels.

8XS5q9xhaMc.summary: A five-minute video showing how to build a counter in the Imba web programming language in under a minute, then style it.
8XS5q9xhaMc.why: HN links it in Imba threads as a quick demonstration of how the language combines code, HTML and CSS.

8dinUbg2h70.summary: Jonathan Blow's GDC talk explains how the time-rewind mechanic in Braid was designed and implemented, including the technical hurdles such as memory limits and state history. It covers both design and engineering concerns.
8dinUbg2h70.why: HN commenters cite it as the reference for how a rewind system works and as a point of comparison for undo and serialization approaches.

8k2AbqTBxao.summary: A short clip of Stephen Fry explaining the differences between American and British comedy. He attributes them to cultural attitudes such as optimism versus pessimism.
8k2AbqTBxao.why: HN commenters cite it as an insightful short explanation of why US and UK comedy differ.

8kUQWuK1L4w.summary: A 1974 talk-show-style interview with the original developers of APL, including Iverson, Falkoff and Breed. They discuss how the language originated.
8kUQWuK1L4w.why: Recommended as a vintage TV segment on APL's origins, and quoted for Iverson's view of APL as notation.

8r1CZTLk-Gk.summary: A clip of Louis C.K.'s bit "Everything's Amazing and Nobody's Happy," about how quickly people take modern technology for granted and complain about it. It is a comedic riff on impatience with air travel and gadgets.
8r1CZTLk-Gk.why: Posted constantly in threads about tech complaints as a reminder to appreciate how remarkable modern technology is.

8rS3fTbC7TE.summary: Patrick Boyle examines SpaceX's planned IPO at a roughly $1.75 trillion valuation. He covers the merging of other Musk companies, orbital data center claims and the fast-track index rules that may help the listing.
8rS3fTbC7TE.why: HN users cite it as the explanation of the tricks around the IPO and the index-inclusion rule changes.

8vJT8AW0wYw.summary: Trailer for the documentary It's Quieter in the Twilight, shown at the Boston SciFi Film Festival. The film follows the engineers who keep the Voyager spacecraft running.
8vJT8AW0wYw.why: Recommended in Voyager threads as a documentary about the team keeping the probes alive.

8xDK2LgSeyk.summary: Curious Droid asks what traces human civilization would leave in the geological record 65 million years from now. It considers how thin the fossil record of humanity might be.
8xDK2LgSeyk.why: HN points to it in discussions of whether a past industrial civilization would leave detectable evidence.

8xFLjUt2leM.summary: Freeman Dyson's 2005 Boston University talk on heretical views about science and society. He questions prevailing dogmas, including his argument that climate and CO2 are a land management issue.
8xFLjUt2leM.why: HN cites it for Dyson's contrarian take on global warming and soil carbon.

84aWtseb2-4.summary: CGP Grey explains the mess of Daylight Saving Time, including its dubious energy savings and the odd cases like Arizona that opt out. It is a short, simple explainer.
84aWtseb2-4.why: HN people link it as the simple go-to explanation of DST and of how irregular time zone rules complicate scheduling.

8Au47gnXs0w.summary: Stuff Made Here builds a device that lets a blind person perceive their surroundings by touch, using an iPad's lidar and a mechanical tactile display driven by motors. The video walks through the build and the limits he hit.
8Au47gnXs0w.why: HN admires the maker's engineering and cites it in accessibility discussions, especially for the limits of sensory resolution versus perception.

8bT6txm4RpA.summary: A 1936 Chevrolet promotional drama, 'Master Hands', showing car manufacturing from foundry to finished vehicle in Flint, Michigan. It is a National Film Registry selection and a record of early mass production.
8bT6txm4RpA.why: HN finds it fascinating as a window into 1930s factory work, often contrasting its hand labor with modern assembly ergonomics.

8wZ1v4PIsYI.summary: Matthias Wandel shows how his pantorouter, a template router machine, works. The flexible machine cuts joints such as mortise and tenon and dovetails, and plans are available.
8wZ1v4PIsYI.why: Cited as a favorite example of clever mechanical design and as a reference for CNC joinery devices.

824yVKUPFjU.summary: Glenn Vanderburg presents Cló, a Clojure library that reimplements TeX's core typesetting algorithms as composable functions. He shows what translating procedural, literate-programming code into functional form teaches.
824yVKUPFjU.why: HN recommends it for its insight into Knuth's TeX algorithms and what changes when they are rewritten functionally.

86x-u-tz0MA.summary: Elizabeth Gilbert, author of Eat, Pray, Love, reflects on the pressure placed on artists to be geniuses. She proposes the older idea that creative people have a genius that visits them rather than being one.
86x-u-tz0MA.why: HN people link it in threads about creativity, late bloomers and creative burnout as a humble, relatable take on where inspiration comes from.

89wq5EoXy-0.summary: A recapture in 50fps HD of Spaceballs' 'State of the Art', an Amiga demo released at The Party 1992. It showcases the Amiga's real-time animation, graphics and music in a few minutes.
89wq5EoXy-0.why: HN uses it as the canonical example of what the demoscene could squeeze out of an Amiga 500 and a single floppy disk.

8Gv0H-vPoDc.summary: Weird Al Yankovic's 2014 parody of 'Blurred Lines' that scolds common grammar and usage errors, with a kinetic typography video. It is a catchy music video about language mistakes.
8Gv0H-vPoDc.why: HN mostly drops it jokingly in threads about grammar, apostrophes and language, and occasionally discusses the animated video's making.

8JKjvY4etTY.summary: Greg Young, who coined CQRS, gives an in-depth GOTO 2014 talk on what event sourcing is, when it is valuable and when it is not, along with its trade-offs and common misconceptions.
8JKjvY4etTY.why: HN commenters list it among the best introductions to event sourcing and use it to illustrate storing read-only events instead of mutating state.

8Q5Nur642BU.summary: A sound-designed restoration of the Miles brothers' 1906 film shot from a cable car down Market Street in San Francisco, four days before the earthquake. It shows streetcars, horse carts, cars and pedestrians mixing freely.
8Q5Nur642BU.why: Cited in street-safety and self-driving threads as a picture of chaotic, shared streets before cars dominated.

8dT6CR9_6l4.summary: GothamChess walks through AlphaZero's famous games against Stockfish, highlighting its unusual pawn sacrifices and positional style. It is aimed at chess fans rather than ML specialists.
8dT6CR9_6l4.why: HN points to it as an entertaining analysis of AlphaZero's play in threads about chess engines.

8eT1jaHmlx8.summary: Jim Keller's talk at the 2020 Scaled Machine Learning conference on Moore's Law in the age of AI chips. He compares scalar, vector and GPU-style parallel approaches to computation.
8eT1jaHmlx8.why: Cited in hardware threads as a Keller talk on the different ways of doing parallel processing.

8moePxHpvok.summary: A short Adam Curtis clip on what he calls oh dearism, the habit of news reporting that presents events as a stream of sad, inexplicable happenings. He argues this leaves viewers passive and unable to imagine action.
8moePxHpvok.why: Shared as a compact critique of how news framing breeds passivity and despair.

8nt3edWLgIg.summary: Sam Harris argues in a TED talk that we will build superhuman AI and have not grappled with the risk of creating something that may treat us the way we treat ants. He makes a logical case for taking AI risk seriously.
8nt3edWLgIg.why: HN cites it in AI risk debates, sometimes as an argument that has aged well and sometimes as an example of alarmist framing.

8pBPZMUcsh0.summary: A short ProPublica video explaining the "Buy, Borrow, Die" strategy wealthy Americans use to cut taxes. They borrow against appreciating assets instead of selling, and the gains are never taxed at death.
8pBPZMUcsh0.why: Shared as a clearer explanation of the tax loophole than the accompanying article.

8q71hrwUcu0.summary: A short clip of Milton Friedman explaining who benefits from occupational licensing requirements, arguing they mainly protect practitioners from competition.
8q71hrwUcu0.why: HN cites it in discussions of occupational licensing and rent-seeking as a libertarian argument.

8s7NmMl_-yg.summary: Hugh Jeffreys tears down the iPhone 13 and assesses its repairability, showing how Apple ties parts like the display and Face ID hardware to specific devices. He demonstrates that swapping parts, even genuine ones, can disable features.
8s7NmMl_-yg.why: HN cites it as evidence of Apple's serialized parts and repair restrictions in threads about right to repair and Face ID disabling.

8-pJa11YvCs.summary: A Startup School SV 2014 conversation between Sequoia's Jim Goetz and WhatsApp founder Jan Koum. They discuss how Sequoia pursued WhatsApp, its tiny engineering team, and how it handled growth and support.
8-pJa11YvCs.why: HN mines it for WhatsApp facts, such as pricing used to slow growth, a 7-8 person backend team and late hiring of customer service.

85OysZ_4lp0.summary: An IIHS car-to-car crash test pitting a 2015 Nissan Tsuru, sold in Mexico, against a 2016 Nissan Versa, sold in the US. It is a 40 mph, 50 percent overlap collision that shows how safety standards differ between markets.
85OysZ_4lp0.why: Cited as a stark demonstration of how much car safety has improved and how regulation differs between countries.

89fYOo1V2pA.summary: A Netflix performance engineer presents how Netflix tunes EC2 instances, covering instance type choice, Xen modes, SR-IOV and kernel tuning. The goal is near bare-metal performance in the cloud.
89fYOo1V2pA.why: HN cites it as an example of workload-dependent performance tuning at scale and of Netflix's AWS practices.

8AyVh1_vWYQ.summary: An Onion News Network satirical segment about a new Sony gadget that is infuriatingly bad, delivered as a profane tech-trends report.
8AyVh1_vWYQ.why: HN mentions it as a joke or a shared favorite Onion classic when tech frustration or The Onion comes up.

8CwoluNRSSc.summary: A short clip parodying Windows Vista's cancel-or-allow security prompts, in the style of Apple's Mac vs PC ads.
8CwoluNRSSc.why: HN mentions it as a joke when Apple's own security prompts or Gatekeeper restrictions annoy users.

8GBAsFwPglw.summary: A 1980 clip of conservative strategist Paul Weyrich telling a religious audience he does not want everybody to vote. He says elections are not won by a majority and that leverage rises as turnout falls.
8GBAsFwPglw.why: HN cites it as a primary-source quote in discussions of voter suppression.

8ISil7IHzxc.summary: A clip of Frank Zappa appearing on CNN's Crossfire in 1986, debating censorship and copyright. Zappa argues his position against record labeling and content restrictions.
8ISil7IHzxc.why: HN commenters invoke it in free speech and censorship debates as a classic example of a articulate defense of free expression.

8JUepj7wIl0.summary: Tom Gally, a former professional translator and University of Tokyo professor, discusses in April 2023 how GPT-4 and similar models may affect translators' careers. He draws on Japanese-English translation experience.
8JUepj7wIl0.why: HN links it as an informed view from a working translator on using GPT for translation.

8P8UKBAOfGo.summary: A two-minute clip of Elon Musk becoming emotional in an interview, reportedly about harsh criticism of SpaceX from astronauts.
8P8UKBAOfGo.why: HN uses it as a reference for Musk's emotional reaction to criticism, not as a recommendation.

8SUkrR7ZfTA.summary: Brian Kernighan's 2009 talk at Princeton on the Elements of Programming Style, discussing readable code, avoiding cleverness and flawed examples in programming tutorials.
8SUkrR7ZfTA.why: HN cites it as the author's own talk on writing clear code, useful as a companion to his book.

8Ux3DKxxFoM.summary: A short clip of President George W. Bush stumbling through the saying 'fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me'.
8Ux3DKxxFoM.why: Used almost entirely as a joke or sarcastic aside about trusting politicians who have lied before.

8VB3uQHa14g.summary: A clip of Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull saying the laws of Australia prevail over the laws of mathematics, regarding encryption. The audio is quiet in the second half.
8VB3uQHa14g.why: HN cites it as a joke and shorthand when governments try to legislate against encryption or math.

8Vq993Td6ys.summary: A short PCWorld news clip from WWDC 2007 in which Steve Jobs announces Safari as the development platform for iPhone apps. Developers could build web apps with access to calling, maps and email.
8Vq993Td6ys.why: HN cites it as evidence that Jobs originally intended web apps to be the iPhone's app model.

8WP7AkJo3OE.summary: A 74-minute video of upgrading Windows 1.0 through every release up to Windows 8 on a real netbook rather than in a virtual machine.
8WP7AkJo3OE.why: HN cites it as the example proving Windows has an unbroken upgrade path from 1.0 to 8.

8mxubNQC5O8.summary: Andreas Kling live-codes a prototype JavaScript JIT compiler for the LibJS engine used in SerenityOS and Ladybird. He builds a standalone bytecode VM, a simple interpreter, and then a simple JIT in about 80 minutes.
8mxubNQC5O8.why: HN commenters cite it as a concrete example of how a skilled developer uses Copilot, mostly as fancy autocomplete for codebase-specific work.

8ucCxtgN6sc.summary: A REACT episode where teenagers try Windows 95 for the first time and react to the retro interface and technology.
8ucCxtgN6sc.why: HN uses it as a light reference for how old software looks to a new generation, often as a half-joke.

8vQmTZTq7nw.summary: AWS's short promo for Snowmobile, a 45-foot shipping container pulled by a semi truck that moves up to 100PB of data to AWS.
8vQmTZTq7nw.why: HN cites it as the example of physically trucking data when network transfer is impractical.

8xRqXYsksFg.summary: A one-minute clip of Scotty from Star Trek giving advice to engineers about managing expectations in estimates. It is a comedic bit of workplace wisdom.
8xRqXYsksFg.why: HN uses it as a joking reference in threads on estimation, technical debt and managing expectations.

8y06NSBBRtY.summary: A three-minute clip of Dwight D. Eisenhower's farewell address of January 17, 1961. In it he warns of the unwarranted influence of the military-industrial complex.
8y06NSBBRtY.why: Cited as a reference whenever threads turn to the NSA, drones, defense contractors or whistleblowers.
